I am getting "Could not load file or assembly 'Oracle.ManagedDataAccess.Kerberos" with Oracle.ManagedDataAccess.Core version 23.26.100 (latest) on my .NET 8 Core app after I changed laptops. It worked fine with the exact same setup. Any ideas?

Q: How do I manage classes in such a way, that I can create as many objects from a class as I need, and not cause a data leak? A:

Because every time you create a new note, you also create a new Image object:

function notesClass:new(id, x, hitTime, speed)
    ...
    note.image = love.graphics.newImage("img/Note_1.png")
    ...
end

But you seem to know that the images should be loaded in the load function:

function game.load()
    ...
    note_image = love.graphics.newImage("img/Note_1.png")
    ...
end

What you need to do is reuse this object, since you have already set notesClass itself as the metatable for each note object, you can simply do this:

function game.load()
    ...
    notesClass.image = love.graphics.newImage("img/Note_1.png")
    ...
end

function notesClass:new(id, x, hitTime, speed)
    ...
    --note.image = love.graphics.newImage("img/Note_1.png")
    ...
end

Q: How to apply role based access control through AD groups in Power apps canvas A:

What data your gallery is displaying?

In power Apps you could use Office365Groups connector to find the Groups and Groups members and check if the login user id exists in the list and then filter your gallery.

ListGroups() will list all the groups.

Office365Groups.ListGroups().value

and ListGroupMembers will list the group members for the group you want, for that you need to provide the group id from the ListGroup(), you can use collection to hold the values.

Office365Groups.ListGroupMembers("your-group-guid").value

Q: Deploying Django backend and React frontend completely free — production-ready options? A:

For hosting Django backend I guess you have many, many options.

I personally use docker image hosted in Azure as App Service. It costs nothing. However I believe you can explore more hosting options here.

So first I would create docker image out of your Django app. For hosting docker images, docker hub is best place, as it's free. Azure container registry costs a lot, as for small project.

Frontend - here you have even more options. I have React frontend app hosted again as docker image on Azure. Same story as above.

However, here you also have other - Vercel or Cloudflare, to name a few.

Both, Vercel and Cloudflare are free.

Here you have list of "React friendly" options for hosting and deployments.

When it comes to database, I have only seen so far only one database hosting, that's free. It's Neon DB, which is Postgres database (you can manage it from web app in browser, or even connect to it with pgAdmin).
